consequence.statement: The CRD upgrade procedure must change from kubectl apply -f manifests/charts/base/files/crd-all.gen.yaml to helm upgrade istio-base. CRD labels will be updated during the first helm upgrade command. Environments that previously used kubectl apply for CRD management must transition to Helm-based management.
consequence.remediation: Change CRD upgrade procedure from kubectl apply to helm upgrade istio-base command for all Helm-based Istio installations.

original.statement: Istio CRDs are now templated by default and managed via Helm; the recommended upgrade method changes from kubectl apply to helm upgrade istio-base, and CRD labels are updated to match Helm-installed resources.

consequence.statement: Nothing fails if the operator does nothing. Upgrading CRDs with `kubectl apply -f manifests/charts/base/files/crd-all.gen.yaml` still works, and `helm upgrade istio-base` is now an allowed way to upgrade CRDs. The labels on Istio CRDs change to be consistent with other Helm-installed resources.
consequence.remediation: Optionally switch CRD upgrades to `helm upgrade istio-base`. Check any tooling that selects or relies on labels of Istio CRDs.

corrected.statement: Istio 1.24.0 templates CRDs in the istio-base chart by default, so they can be upgraded with `helm upgrade istio-base`. CRD labels change to match other Helm-installed resources. Upgrading CRDs with `kubectl apply` still works, so this is a behavior change to review, not a required migration.

decision.reason: [ev-85eccdc718e3] and [ev-2941a875a468] describe `helm upgrade istio-base` as something the change "allows". The change text also says operators who used `kubectl apply` "can continue to do so", so nothing is described as a required step. The only change that happens without any operator action is that CRD labels now match other Helm-installed resources. The CRDs still work after that, so this is a behavior-change to review, not migration-required.
